claims.text: Varying elemental composition can tune the magnetic properties of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Varying elemental composition can tune the magnetocaloric properties of non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
The initial material is a low-dimensional, non-equiatomic HEA containing both magnetic and non-magnetic elements.
Controlled variation of elemental concentrations is the proposed tuning intervention.
Changing elemental ratios induces local lattice distortions.
Changing elemental ratios alters chemical ordering.
Changing the relative concentrations of constituent elements modifies local magnetic exchange interactions.
Changing the relative concentrations of constituent elements modifies electron concentration.
Modified magnetic exchange interactions and electron concentration shift the magnetic ordering temperature.
Modified magnetic exchange interactions and electron concentration alter the magnetic entropy change.
Increasing or decreasing the fraction of magnetic elements will produce a predictable shift in magnetic transition temperature.
Increasing or decreasing the fraction of magnetic elements will change the magnitude of the magnetic entropy change.
Significant tuning effects are expected only over a compositional range that preserves a single-phase or controlled multiphase structure.
Extreme compositional deviations may cause phase separation.
The magnitude of magnetic and magnetocaloric changes depends on the selected elements and their interactions.
Processing conditions and dimensional constraints may affect the magnitude of the response.
